details: CONFIRMED by reading: checker.md "Write is only for your input file (a scratchpad or the worktree's `.ci/`)."
critic.md "Write is only for the TOML input file". Precedence part: "the project's rules for this agent win,
then the project's rules for your role, then the text of your flow in this file, then the shared text of your
role." The new rule sits in the shared text, the lowest rank. Whether a model actually skips the sketch is
PLAUSIBLE (no eval, see F2), but the text the item adds is the weakest of three conflicting texts.
Size: 10 agent minutes (two flow lines, one base line, relay sync, the text test).
evidence: -> "Write is only for your input file (a scratchpad or the worktree's `.ci/`). You never write a check mark"
critic.md flow: "Write is only for the TOML input file; `relay check record review --input <file>` writes ..."
grep -n 'Bash is for reading' roles/judge.md -> 25:- Bash is for reading, and for running one existing test or check that
failing_case: A checker gets a finding whose failing case is "strip_marks('[a]_`b`') keeps the brackets". The base (step 2)
now says: run it as a scratch script in the scratchpad. Its own flow part says "Write is only for your input
file (a scratchpad or the worktree's .ci/)", and the precedence part says the flow text wins over the shared
role text; the base Scope bullet also says "Bash is for reading, and for running one existing test or check".
Now: two instructions that forbid writing the script outrank the one that requires it; a checker that obeys
precedence reads and marks MET (the very failure of the item). Should: the flow part allows the sketch file.
fix_hint: checker.md: "Write is only for your input file and a check-step-2 sketch script, both in the scratchpad (or
the input in the worktree's .ci/)". Same in critic.md. In the judge base Scope bullet add "and, in check mode,
a sketch of a failing case (check step 2)". Extend the new test to assert the flow lines.
pass_cases: 1. checker.md flow part: the Write sentence names a scratch sketch script in the scratchpad beside the input file.
2. critic.md flow part ("Write is only for the TOML input file"): same allowance, since the critic carries check mode too.
3. roles/judge.md Scope bullet "Bash is for reading, and for running one existing test" names the check-mode sketch as allowed (or is scoped to review mode), in all five synced copies.
4. The checker still may not write in the worktree outside .ci/ (the sketch is outside the repo).
reason: tests/test_roles.py test_check_flow_parts_allow_the_scratch_script passes; checker.md and critic.md unchanged since the earlier check.

details: CONFIRMED by reading SKILL.md lines 71-83 and plugins/openspec/skills/plan/SKILL.md:66-75. Correct today in

evidence: sed -n 60,100p plugins/openspec/skills/spec-review/SKILL.md -> "says so in its verdict" ... "The spec check writes no verdict"
failing_case: spec-review step 4, the path the item is about: "the checker runs that sketch ... and says so in its verdict",
and a few lines down "The spec check writes no verdict (it is not a merge)"; the checker flow: with
`Gate: none (artifacts only)` "the report writes no verdict ... a plain text file". The base says "say so in
the verdict reason". In openspec, plan/SKILL.md uses "sketch" for the picture saved in
openspec/changes/<change>/sketch/. Now: a checker of a spec review has no verdict reason to write into and
"that sketch" can be read as the saved design sketch. Should: "says so in the report's line for that finding
(sketch run: ...)", and a word not taken in openspec (a probe script).
fix_hint: "... the checker runs it as a scratch script outside the repo and writes `sketch run: <what it showed>` on
that finding's line of its report". Optionally say "probe" instead of "sketch" in both texts.
pass_cases: 1. SKILL.md step 4 names where the sketch result goes in the plain-text spec-check report.
2. The base's "verdict reason" wording also covers the plain-text report (or names it).
3. The word used for the script is not "sketch" in the openspec plugin, or is qualified ("a scratch script").
reason: Wording test in tests/test_roles.py passes; unchanged since the earlier check.
